tools.name: tinypng_compress_image
tools.description: WRITE (uses quota): ask TinyPNG (Tinify) to fetch a public image by URL and compress it (JPEG, PNG, WebP, AVIF or JPEG XL). tools.name: tinypng_transform_image
tools.description: WRITE (uses quota): apply a resize, a format conversion and/or metadata preservation to an image compressed earlier (the output_url from tinypng_compress_image, valid about 48 hours). Returns the resulting type, byte size, width, height and Compression-Count; the image itself is returned too when in

tools.name: tinypng_download_image
tools.description: Fetch the compressed image of an earlier tinypng_compress_image (its output_url, valid about 48 hours) and return it as an image with its type, byte size, width and height. Images over 1 MB are described but not returned inline. Downloading does not use extra compression quota. GET /output/{id}.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: tinypng_compress_image, tinypng_get_usage · Private data: tinypng_compress_image, tinypng_transform_image, tinypng_get_usage · Public sink: tinypng_compress_image, tinypng_transform_image, tinypng_get_usage · Destructive: tinypng_transform_image.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: tinypng_compress_image, tinypng_get_usage · Private data: tinypng_compress_image, tinypng_transform_image, tinypng_get_usage · Public sink: tinypng_compress_image, tinypng_transform_image, tinypng_get_usage · Destructive: tinypng_transform_image

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
